abstract: Many discussions inside the broadcasting community are focused on next-generation broadcast formats. For content producers and distributors, the primary question remains: What will be the best solution for the next-generation broadcast format? Is it just the double pixel count in horizontal and vertical directions? Will a higher frame rate, a higher dynamic range and extended color range, or both provide viewers with a higher value? Or which combination of these improvements needs to be included in a next-generation broadcast format? The answer will likely depend on the type of production, type of content delivery, or both. All of these points have a direct influence on imager technology, and this paper explains the different potential solutions of “4K” or ultrahigh-definition image acquisition, including their strengths and limitations, with a focus on live broadcast productions.

authors.bio: Klaus Weber is responsible for the worldwide product marketing of the imaging products for Grass Valley, A Belden Brand. The imaging products include all of the LDX Camera Systems used in a wide range of broadcast application.Weber’s past experience includes customer support, technical and operational training, and regional sales management for broadcast cameras. He has more than 30 years of industry experience, with the past 20 focused on various duties around marketing and business development for the Grass Valley camera factory in Breda, The Netherlands. He is the author of several technical articles and white papers addressing the different camera related technologies and topics.Weber has also presented several technical papers at various industry events, as well as participating in industry round table discussions in many different countries around the world.
